newsitem.title: BELGIUM: LIEGE AIMS TO TAKE BUSINESS FROM DUTCH AIRPORTS.
newsitem.headline: LIEGE AIMS TO TAKE BUSINESS FROM DUTCH AIRPORTS.

text.p: Belgium's Liege airport is aiming to attract business away from Dutch airports as the Netherlands tightens its aviation regulations.
Luc Partoune, the airport's managing director, said Liege would target both cargo and charter airlines currently using Maastricht and Schiphol airports in the Netherlands.
Currently Turkish Airlines and Iberia are two carriers using Maastricht Aachen Airport in the south of the Netherlands for their cargo activities.
But recently the Dutch said the airport would only have restricted night flights.
The airport will only be able to have 900 aircraft movements a year and this is thought to restrict cargo and charter operators, sources said.
Carriers, such as Dutch cargo and charter carrier Martinair, have stressed the importance of an airport having a 24-hour operation before it decides to operate from an airport.
"Liege operates 24 hours a day and we are only 30 km from Maastricht," said Partoune. "We are also looking to develop our passenger charter business."
Schiphol also announced it would be toughening measures concerning Chapter 2 aircraft and it would not be allowing any more operators of these aircraft into the airport.
Partoune said: "Liege can handle the largest aircraft, including Antonov 124s and Boeing 747s and the area is less populated so it does not affect the local residents quite so much."
